subject: ventures/pipedrive-import-csv-check
professional: a RevOps / CRM administrator who migrates customers into Pipedrive with the spreadsheet importer. First checks: the mandatory fields per item (person name, organization name, deal linked to a person or organization), the 50 MB / 50,000-row caps, deal status and currency format, date layout, and whether the tool reads an ordinary people or deals file as the right kind

evidence.correctness: Ran the shipped validate()/repair() on 11 probe files (scratchpad probe.mjs, cases in checks) and compared with Pipedrive's import help as quoted by WebSearch (support.pipedrive.com itself would not resolve from this session, so no direct page load). Right: 50 MB cap, currency symbols rejected, mixed DMY/MDY and impossible dates, case-insensitive duplicate emails, scientific-notation phones, repair is formatting only. Wrong: a deals file with no Person or Organization gets no error although Pipedrive's mandatory-fields article says such deals are skipped; the row limit is 100,000 against the documented 50,000; 'Name,Organization' people files and 'Title,Organization,Status' deal files are auto-detected as organizations, producing false warnings and skipping the status check; Pipedrive-export style 'Person - Name' headings give a false 'No Name column' error. 5 of 9 correctness checks pass: 2.
evidence.completeness: Every check the README lists fires on a probe file, the three samples load, repair lists each change with its line, findings CSV and NOT_CHECKED travel with the result (tests). Page wiring checked by page.test.mjs; page not loaded in a browser. No stubs or TODOs: 3.
evidence.verification: `node --test '*.test.mjs'` in the subject root: 31/31 pass (includes a seeded fuzz of repair idempotence). 8 mutants via quality_mutate.py: 3 caught, 5 survive (probability boundary, ROW_LIMIT, duplicate-deal key, plain-number regex accepting commas, DMY/MDY labels). The tests encode the author's rules, so the wrong row limit and the missing deal-link rule could not be caught: 2.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (535 lines), calc.test.mjs, repair-fuzz.test.mjs, usage.mjs and index.html. Pure, dependency-free, a real CSV parser with line tracking, header resolution by exact/spelling/alias/edit distance. Defects: chooseKind's ordered keyword lists are brittle (no 'title'/'status' deal signal, 'organization' is an org signal even beside 'name' in a people file); the alias tables silently map 'Organization' to 'Name' in org kind; very long single-line statements. A senior JS reviewer would accept it with the detection fix: 3.
evidence.claims: Disclaimer (no warranty, not advice, not affiliated, nominative trademark), from-memory caveat, privacy text and local-only usage counting with opt-out and DNT/GPC are present and tested; served llms.txt/sitemap clean (served-copy.mjs). But the rules list states 'a deal needs a title' (Pipedrive: a linked person or organization) and the warning text 'about 100,000' rows (Pipedrive: 50,000); '0.6 is read as 0.6 percent' is unhedged and unsourced. The from-memory hedge discloses but does not back them: 2.
evidence.fitness: Walked a migration: paste a deals export with Title, Value, Currency, Status, Stage. The tool catches the spreadsheet damage (symbols, sci notation, bad dates, status words) well. But a deals file without a person/org column is passed clean and then skipped by Pipedrive, a file between 50,000 and 100,000 rows is passed, and a plain people file with an Organization column is misread unless the user changes the dropdown. A CRM admin would hit at least one of these in the first hour: 2.
evidence.domain: Compared with Pipedrive's import help (mandatory fields, limits, skip-file reasons) as quoted by search: status Open/Won/Lost, ISO currency, integer IDs, date-format choice at mapping and the skip-file behaviour are in line; departures are the deal-link mandatory rule, the 50,000-row cap, ID severity, and no recognition of Pipedrive's own '<Item> - <Field>' column names. Two core rules wrong: 2.

defects.what: Deals are not checked for a linked Person or Organization. Pipedrive's mandatory-fields article says a deal row needs a person name or an organization name, or it lands in the skip file; the tool requires only Title (REQUIRED.deals = ['title']), gives a deals file with neither column a clean result, and the page tells users 'a deal needs a title'.

Auto-detection misreads common files. 'Name,Organization' (a people file, the README's own example headings) is read as organizations with a false 'Name appears in two columns' warning; 'Title,Organization,Status' deals are read as organizations, so 'Closed Won' is never checked and every deal is flagged as a duplicate organization. chooseKind tests deal headings first, then people headings without 'name'/'organization', then treats 'organization' or 'name' as an organizations file, and never treats 'title' or 'status' as a deal signal. The kind dropdown defaults to auto.
Row limit is 100,000; Pipedrive's import help states 50,000 rows per spreadsheet. A 60,000-row file gets no warning. The warning text also says 'about 100,000'.

Headings in Pipedrive's own '<Item> - <Field>' export style ('Person - Name', 'Deal - Title', 'Organization - Name') are not recognised: a re-imported Pipedrive export gets a false 'No Name column' error. Unconfirmed against the live importer (support site unreachable this session).

5 of 8 seeded mutants survive: the probability-fraction boundary, the row limit constant (the only test passes rowLimit:1), the duplicate-deal key, the plain-number regex and the DMY/MDY labelling are unpinned. No test covers kind auto-detection of a people file with an Organization column, or a deal with no person/organization.
Non-integer ID is a warning, but Pipedrive's skip-file help says such rows are skipped; it should be an error.
'Pipedrive reads 0.6 as 0.6 percent' is stated without a hedge or source on the page and README; no Pipedrive document found backs it.

verdict: A careful spreadsheet-damage checker that gets the generic faults right (currency symbols, Excel scientific notation, mixed day/month dates, impossible dates, duplicate emails, formatting-only repair) but misses Pipedrive's own rules where they matter: deals without a linked Person or Organization, which Pipedrive's mandatory-fields help says are skipped, pass clean; the row cap is 100,000 against the documented 50,000; and auto-detection reads an ordinary 'Name,Organization' people file, or a 'Title,Organization,Status' deals file, as organizations, with false warnings and the status check skipped. 31/31 tests pass but 5 of 8 seeded mutants survive. Scores: correctness 2, completeness 3, verification 2, craft 3, claims 2, fitness 2, domain 2. Finished, does not meet the bar. Pipedrive's help site could not be fetched directly from this session; the rules are as quoted by web search.
